knowledge:
- key_parameters: fracTable=A numeric matrix containing tumor fraction estimates (CCFs) for all clones (rows) at all time points (columns) ;; parents=An integer vector specifying parental relationships between clones (0 represents normal cell/origin) ;; timepoints=A numeric vector specifying the time points for each column of the fraction matrix ;; timepointInterpolation=Boolean; if TRUE, interpolates extra time points to improve visualization (highly recommended when having fewer time points than clones) ;; therapyEffect=A single numeric value or two-element vector indicating when to estimate therapy effect ;; pos=Plotting position of clones in dolphin/combined plots ('center' or 'bottom') ;; clonesToFill=An integer vector in plaicePlot to color clones representing bi-allelic events
- alternatives: timescape (an established R package for clonal evolution visualization; clevRvis revised and optimized its features, supporting branched independent evolution, single clone visualization, and bottom/centered layouts)
- when_to_use: When analyzing tumor heterogeneity and clonal evolution over multiple time points, specifically when you have clustered mutations into clones, calculated CCFs, and reconstructed phylogenetic trees.
- pitfalls: If there is only one measured time point, time point interpolation is needed and the time point of origin must be manually specified (originTimepoint) ;; Extended shark plots (extSharkPlot) and dolphin plots (dolphinPlot) cannot be visualized together in combinedPlot ;; Automatic clustering and tree reconstruction algorithms for bulk DNA-seq data do not always generate valid results; manual analysis/curation is suggested before using clevRvis ;; A maximum of 20,000 parental relations is investigated in exploreTrees.

workflows.name: standard_clonal_visualization
workflows.intent: Create a seaObject from clone fractions and parental relations, optionally interpolate timepoints or estimate therapy effects, and visualize using shark, dolphin, or combined plots.
workflows.stages: 1. Create seaObject with or without timepoint interpolation and therapy effect estimation ;; 2. Generate basic or extended shark plots ;; 3. Generate detailed dolphin plots ;; 4. Generate linked interactive combined plots
workflows.code:
timepoints <- c(0,50,100)
parents <- c(0,1,1,3,0,5,6)
fracTable <- matrix(c(20,10,0,0,0,0,0,
                    40,20,15,0,30,10,0,
                    50,25,15,10,40,20,15),
                    ncol = length(timepoints))
seaObject <- createSeaObject(fracTable, parents, timepoints,
                            timepointInterpolation = FALSE)

##seaObject with enabled time point estimation
seaObject_tp <- createSeaObject(fracTable, parents, timepoints,
                                timepointInterpolation = TRUE)

##seaObject with enabled time point estimation and therapy effect 
##estimation between time point 50 and 100
seaObject_te <- createSeaObject(fracTable, parents, timepoints,
                            timepointInterpolation = TRUE,
                            therapyEffect = c(50,100))

##seaObject with manually defined colors
seaObject_col <- createSeaObject(fracTable, parents, timepoints,
                                timepointInterpolation = TRUE,
                                col = rainbow(7))

#Basic shark plot showing legend and title
sharkPlot(seaObject_tp, showLegend = TRUE, main = 'Example Shark plot')

#Basic shark plot showing legend and title with manually defined color coding
sharkPlot(seaObject_col, showLegend = TRUE, main = 'Example Shark plot')

##extended shark plot, showing CCF as point size only for measured 
###time points, legend and title
extSharkPlot(seaObject_tp, timepoints = timepoints, showLegend = TRUE, 
            main = 'Example Extended Shark plot')

##Dolphin plot, with vertical lines showing all time points, custom y axis 
##label and triangles indicating the measured time points
dolphinPlot(seaObject_tp, showLegend = TRUE, 
            vlines = timepoints(seaObject), 
            vlab = timepoints(seaObject), vlabSize = 2, 
            ylab = 'Cancer cell fractions (CCFs)',
            markMeasuredTimepoints = timepoints)

##Dolphin plot polygon shape
dolphinPlot(seaObject_tp, showLegend = TRUE, vlines = timepoints,
            vlab = timepoints, vlabSize = 2, 
            ylab = 'Cancer cell fractions (CCFs)', shape = 'polygon')

##Dolphin plot bottom layout and separated independent clones
dolphinPlot(seaObject_tp, showLegend = FALSE,  vlines = timepoints,
            vlab = timepoints, vlabSize = 2, 
            ylab = 'Cancer cell fractions (CCFs)', 
            separateIndependentClones = TRUE, pos = 'bottom')

##Dolphin plot with annotations
annotsTable <- data.frame(x = c(50,75), y = c(15,50), 
                            col = c('black', 'white'), 
                            lab = c('Annotation clone 5', 'Annotation clone 2'))
dolphinPlot(seaObject_tp, showLegend = TRUE, main = 'Example Dolphin Plot', 
            vlines = timepoints, vlab = timepoints, vlabSize = 2, 
            ylab = 'Cancer cell fraction', annotations = annotsTable, 
            pos = 'bottom', separateIndependentClones = TRUE)

##Dolphin plot with enabled therapy effect estimation
##vertical lines show all time points, customized y axis label,
##triangles indicate the measured time points
dolphinPlot(seaObject_te, showLegend = TRUE, 
            vlines = slot(seaObject,"timepoints"), 
            vlab = slot(seaObject,"timepoints"), vlabSize = 2, 
            ylab = 'Cancer cell fractions (CCFs)',
            markMeasuredTimepoints = timepoints)

##Basic shark plot linked to dolphin plot
combinedPlot(seaObject_tp, showLegend = TRUE, vlines = timepoints,
            vlab = timepoints, vlabSize = 2, ylab = 'Cancer cell fraction',
            separateIndependentClones = TRUE)

workflows.name: allele_aware_visualization
workflows.intent: Generate an allele-aware visualization (plaice plot) showing clonal evolution alongside bi-allelic events and remaining healthy alleles over time.
workflows.stages: 1. Create seaObject with timepoint interpolation or therapy effect estimation ;; 2. Generate plaice plots with optional annotations and custom clone coloring to represent bi-allelic events
workflows.code:
timepoints <- c(0,50,100)
parents <- c(0,1,1,3,0,5,6)
fracTable <- matrix(c(20,10,0,0,0,0,0,
                    40,20,15,0,30,10,0,
                    50,25,15,10,40,20,15),
                    ncol = length(timepoints))
seaObject_tp <- createSeaObject(fracTable, parents, timepoints,
                                timepointInterpolation = TRUE)
seaObject_te <- createSeaObject(fracTable, parents, timepoints,
                            timepointInterpolation = TRUE,
                            therapyEffect = c(50,100))

#Plaice plot when all genes have at least one healthy copy
plaicePlot(seaObject_tp, showLegend = TRUE,  vlines = timepoints,
            vlab = timepoints, vlabSize = 4, ylab = TRUE, 
            separateIndependentClones = TRUE)

#Plaice plot showing biallelic events + annotations
annotsTable <- data.frame(x = c(24,55), y = c(-40,-5), 
                            col = c('black', 'white'), 
                            lab = c('TP53', 'UBA1'))
plaicePlot(seaObject_tp, showLegend = TRUE,  vlines = timepoints,
            vlab = timepoints, vlabSize = 4, ylab = TRUE, 
            separateIndependentClones = TRUE, clonesToFill = c(0,0,1,0,0,6,0),
            annotations = annotsTable)

##Plaice plot with enabled therapy effect estimation, 
##all genes are assumed to have at least one healthy copy
plaicePlot(seaObject_te, showLegend = TRUE,  vlines = timepoints,
            vlab = timepoints, vlabSize = 4, ylab = TRUE, 
            separateIndependentClones = TRUE)

workflows.name: explore_alternative_trees
workflows.intent: Determine all valid parental relations based on clone fractions and timepoints to explore alternative phylogenetic trees.
workflows.stages: 1. Define clone fractions and timepoints ;; 2. Run exploreTrees to find valid parental relations
workflows.code:
timepoints <- c(0,30,75,150)
fracTable <- matrix(
            c( 100, 45, 00, 00,
                20, 00, 00, 00,
                30, 00, 20, 05,
                98, 00, 55, 40),
            ncol=length(timepoints))

trees <- exploreTrees(fracTable, timepoints)
trees
